papers.title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
papers.abstract: An agent framework that turns text instructions or reference videos into executable 3D camera paths, using Director, Interpreter, Scout, and Critic agents and a new benchmark, CinemaBench.

papers.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Agents can combine facts from several confidential documents into a forbidden conclusion. Tests show this leak persists at notable rates even with classification headers and aggregation rules.

papers.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: T2Quant allocates activation precision across diffusion denoising steps using a label-free sensitivity signal, improving accuracy under a fixed bit budget by up to 6.7 points.

papers.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
papers.abstract: A benchmark where AI agents design compact evaluators. The best ones rank candidate model pairs like target benchmarks about 75% of the time, below a 91% ceiling.

papers.title: RTAformer: Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer for Video Scene Graph Generation
papers.abstract: A one-stage transformer that models entity persistence and relation changes separately to fix stale predictions in video scene graphs, improving recall on Action Genome.

papers.title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
papers.abstract: A framework with a 14-type taxonomy for detecting research integrity violations in agent trajectories, plus runtime correction that cuts remaining violations by 36.8%.

papers.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
papers.abstract: Gives coding agents a LEGO assembly API and physics validator, reaching 100% physical validity on 512 prompts while keeping prompt adherence.

papers.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
papers.abstract: A framework that records attacker setup and scoring rules so privacy attacks on split LLMs can be compared, and requires an undefended baseline before a defense can pass.

papers.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
papers.abstract: Diffusion LMs spend more forward passes on novel or rare output and less on copied text. Decoding effort also tracks correctness, and speed-weighted voting beats majority voting.

papers.title: HyperDrone: Simulation-to-Reality Transfer at Millions of Frames per Second
papers.abstract: A GPU quadrotor simulator with a ray-tracing renderer running at millions of frames per second, used to train a vision-based policy that transfers to a real Crazyflie drone.

cc_updates.body:
What's changed
* Added the Monitor tool and plugin monitors on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry, and when telemetry or nonessential traffic is disabled; long foreground sleeps are now blocked there too
* Fixed requests failing behind some gateways and compatible servers that reject the effort-2025-11-24 beta value or mid-conversation system messages; Claude Code now retries without them
* Fixed background cleanup deleting some recent files, such as pasted images, when cleanupPeriodDays is set to a very large value

What's changed
* Fixed sandboxed Bash commands on macOS and Linux running the shell's startup files outside the sandbox before each command
* Fixed macOS sandbox denyWrite glob patterns not applying at a path's real location when the pattern's folder is reached through a symlink
* Fixed sandboxed commands and auto-accepted edits being able to modify the MCP config file passed with --mcp-config
* Fixed a disabled MCP server being reconnected by a later permission prompt in print and SDK sessions

What's changed
* Bug fixes and reliability improvements
